frozen: Committed before the held-out split ran. The development split ran twice while the policies and the study were built (scratch runs, not records): the first found the full feedback worse than none, because the thirst search overrode foraging and fruit juice is water too, which led to thirst yielding to hunger; the second showed the full feedback improving hydration (+0.07 over no feedback, +0.10 over the heat-only arm, +0.08 over the displaced-humidity arm) but not survival (0.75 for both), because survival in one environment was decided by food the feedback does not reach. On that basis, and before any held-out run, the primary endpoint was set to hydration, the variable the feedback regulates; survival stays a pre-registered criterion with its 0.25 minimum effect.
question: Do homeostatic feedback policies (thirst-driven humidity search and drinking; heat-driven escape from the light and rest in shade) keep a mortal research fly in the deployed configuration alive and hydrated in a hot, dry walled yard, and is the benefit attributable to the feedback and to the humidity sense it reads?
status: A seeded study on disposable research subjects, not a registered R.A.I.N. experiment. No subject is Eva or ECHO, a copy or a continuation; Eva and ECHO cannot die and nothing here reaches them.

arms.deployed: The deployed configuration with its artificial maintenance (cannot die). A non-biological reference, never a comparator.
arms.full: Mortal body, thirst and heat policies. Primary arm.
arms.no-thirst: Mortal body, heat policy only (thirst ablated).
arms.no-heat: Mortal body, thirst policy only (heat ablated).
arms.shuffled-humidity: Mortal body, both policies, the humidity sense read at a fixed point 7 m away (folded into the yard): the policy's activity kept, its link to the fly's place broken. Water underfoot is still sensed where the fly is.

endpoints: Alive at the horizon; hours lived; hydrated share (time alive with body water >= 0.7, over time alive); hours with body above 32 C.

bootstrap.rule: Paired percentile bootstrap over environments (every fly of a drawn environment kept); 95% interval.

criteria.rule: Held-out: the interval of hydrated share(full) - hydrated share(no-feedback) excludes 0 (above): the feedback keeps a mortal fly hydrated.
Held-out: the interval of hydrated share(full) - hydrated share(no-thirst) excludes 0 (above): the thirst feedback is what does it.
Held-out: the interval of hydrated share(full) - hydrated share(shuffled-humidity) excludes 0 (above): the humidity sense, not activity, matters.
Held-out: survival(full) - survival(no-feedback) >= 0.25 and its interval excludes 0.
Held-out: the interval of hours hot(full) - hours hot(no-heat) excludes 0 (below): the heat feedback keeps it cooler.
Held-out: the median hydrated share of the full arm >= 0.8.
